title: Lesson 6: Close Read-aloud, Session 4 and Role-Playing: Summer Sun Risin'
objective: Students describe what the boy and the sun do at the end of the story Summer Sun Risin' through close reading, discussion, role-play, and writing.

what_is_taught.skill: describe what characters do at the end of a story
retell important events from a story
use sentence frames to discuss story events
participate in partner discussions about story content
role-play story events to deepen understanding
reflect on and discuss respectful behavior during partner work
write and draw about story events using key details
use classroom resources to support writing (word walls, high-frequency word lists, alphabet charts)
define and explain vocabulary related to story setting (e.g., sunset, setting)
use Think-Pair-Share protocol to discuss story and personal experiences
practice a movement routine (Sun Movement routine)

what_is_NOT_taught: complex vocabulary instruction beyond basic definitions

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify story events and vocabulary during partner and group discussions
student_actions.oral_production: participate orally in partner discussions, role-play, and whole group sharing
student_actions.written_production: write and draw about story events on response sheets
student_actions.procedural_application: practice the Sun Movement routine steps
student_actions.representation_modeling: model the Sun Movement routine steps and role-play story events
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain meanings of story chunks and vocabulary words using sentence frames and partner talk
student_actions.comprehension_response: respond to questions about story events and setting during discussions and close read-aloud sessions, including retelling events in sequence and describing character actions and setting details, using key details from the text and pictures, both orally and in writing, with some use of sentence frames and partner talk to support responses, and participate in Think-Pair-Share discussions about personal experiences related to the story setting and events, using sentence stems as needed to elaborate or repeat classmates' ideas, and reflect on respectful behavior during partner work protocols, including role-play and Think-Pair-Share protocols, to deepen understanding of story content and social skills.

evidence.quote: Invite students to stand up and spread out inside and around the edge of the whole group meeting area. As needed, remind students to move safely and make space for everyone.
Remind students that in Lesson 4, they learned the rest of the steps to the Sun Movement routine. Review the steps on the Sun Movement chart.
Invite students to join you as you practice Steps 1-10, taking 10-15 seconds for each step.
When reviewing the Sun Movement routine, foster community by inviting a few student volunteers to model Steps 1-10 for the class. (MME)
Direct students' attention to the posted learning target and read it aloud: 'I can describe what the boy and the sun do at the end of Summer Sun Risin'. '
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner: 'What time of day do you think the end of the story takes place?' (at the end of the day)
'Where do you think the sun will be at the end of the story?' (at one corner of the page)
Invite students to take out their magic bows and take aim at the target.
Guide students through the close read-aloud for Summer Sun Risin' using the Close Readaloud Guide: Summer Sun Risin' (Session 4; for teacher reference).

To activate background knowledge before students discuss what the boy and sun do in the end of Summer Sun Risin', invite students to reflect on the relationship based on what they know about the beginning and middle of the story. (Example: 'Think back to what the boy and sun were doing at the beginning and middle of the story. With your partner, discuss why you think the sun will be at one corner of the page at the end of the story. What have you learned from the story so far that makes you think this might be the case?') (MMR)

For ELLs: Mini Language Dive. Ask students about the meaning of the chunks from the text: 'Pa by the door, / me tucked in bed. / Summer sun's sleepin', / stars overhead.' from Summer Sun Risin.' Write and display student responses next to the chunks.
'What does this verse mean?' (Responses will vary.)
'What is Pa doing?' (Pa is playing guitar and singing by the door.)
'What does the word by mean in this chunk?' (next to)
'What is the boy doing?' (sleeping; lying in bed)
'What is the sun doing?' (It is gone because it is night time.'
'Where are the stars?' (in the sky; overhead)
'What two words do you see in overhead? What do you think overhead means? Point to something overhead.' (over + head; up above our heads)
'Now what do you think the verse means? (Responses will vary.)'
-'Discuss with a partner what the boy and sun are doing using the frame: In the end, the boy is _____. The sun is _____.' (sleeping; gone or set)

Offer students specific feedback on their close-reading skills used to explore the focus question: 'What is the boy doing when the sun is setting in the sky?' (Example: 'Everyone looked closely at the pictures and noticed that the sun was moving down on the page and that the boy was reading a story with his dad and getting ready for bed.')
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group: 'What does it mean when the sun is setting?' (The sun is going down.)
Invite students to create an accompanying hand gesture as they repeat the word with you.

Tell students that later in today's lesson they will be writing and drawing about the ending events so today they will continue to think about, discuss, and role-play these events with a partner so they better understand them in order to do their best writing.
Move students into pre-determined pairs and tell them they are going to use the Role-Play protocol to act out a few of the ending events of Summer Sun Risin.'
Remind students to focus on showing respect while working with their partner during the protocol.
Invite students to begin the Role-Play protocol for the following sections of text:
Tell students they are going to use the Think-Pair-Share protocol to discuss how they showed respect during the Role-Play protocol.
Invite them to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner: 'What did it look and sound like when you were showing respect during the Role-Play protocol?'
Offer the following sentence stems as necessary:
Gather students back together and invite a few students to share out.
Display Part II of the Summer Sun Risin' response sheet and read the directions aloud.

Remind students that yesterday they began Part II by writing and drawing about the beginning and middle events using key details from the text. Tell them that today they will complete the response sheet by writing and drawing about the ending events of the story.
Direct students' attention to the last box. As you point to the box, read the sentence frame. ('At the end …')
Remind students to think about the parts they acted out for the ending of the story when completing today's writing task.
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:
Invite students to show a thumbs-up or touch their head if they are ready to begin writing and drawing about the events from the ending of Summer Sun Risin'.
Point out the Summer Sun Risin' response sheets and pencils already at student workspaces. Transition students their workspaces and invite them to begin working.
Circulate and support students as necessary. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts).

After 5 minutes, signal all students to stop working. Model cleanup. Invite students to walk safely to the whole group gathering area. Collect student response sheets and offer specific, positive feedback on their writing and drawing. (Example: 'I noticed that Samantha and Jose used pictures and words to describe events from the ending of the story.')
Gather students together whole group.
Define setting (moving down).
Tell students they are going to use the Think-Pair-Share protocol to discuss what the boy experiences during sunset and what they experience during sunset.
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner: 'Where is the sun at sunset?' (The sun is starting to disappear in the sky.)
'What does the boy experience when the sun is setting?' (The boy is reading a book with his dad and getting ready for bed.)
'What do you experience when the sun is setting?' (I get ready for bed.)
Offer the following sentence stem as necessary: 'When the sun is setting (the sun/the boy/I) _________.'
Gather students back together and invite a few students to share with the whole group.

If time permits, cue students to expand the conversation by saying more and to listen carefully: 'Can you say more about that?' (Responses will vary.) 'Who can repeat what your classmate said?' (Responses will vary.)

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Models the Sun Movement routine steps; reads aloud learning targets and sentence frames; models use of response sheets; reviews and models partner discussion and role-play protocols; defines vocabulary (setting); models Think-Pair-Share protocol.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What time of day do you think the end of the story takes place?
Where do you think the sun will be at the end of the story?
What does the word by mean in this chunk?
What two words do you see in overhead? What do you think overhead means? Point to something overhead.
What does it mean when the sun is setting?
What did it look and sound like when you were showing respect during the Role-Play protocol?
Where is the sun at sunset?
What does the boy experience when the sun is setting?
What do you experience when the sun is setting?
Can you say more about that?
Who can repeat what your classmate said?

scope.depth: focus on describing and retelling ending events with key details, using sentence frames and partner talk, practicing respectful behavior, and writing/drawing about story events

notes: Lesson focuses on comprehension of story ending through multiple modalities including oral discussion, role-play, and writing. Vocabulary related to setting (sunset, setting) is taught with definitions and gestures. Respectful collaboration is emphasized during partner work. Supports for ELLs and diverse learners are integrated.
